title: Session途中で追加された要求が直前実装の約2倍規模の編集無効化を引き起こし、要求の事前予告でもReworkが削減されない
summary: Mining of 3,553 real-world coding-agent sessions (SWE-chat) shows that when a user introduces a new requirement after implementation has begun, the requirement's arrival is followed by roughly twice as much invalidation of prior edits as matched non-requirement turns, and the rework burden persists at all session stages. A controlled experiment found that disclosing the upcoming requirement in advance produced no measurable reduction in code overwriting — agents implement eagerly and cannot hold back work for announced-but-inactive constraints. This makes late requirement emergence a quantified, structural driver of wasted agent work and code churn distinct from initial requirement ambiguity (A01) or cross-artifact propagation failure (A07): the failure is the agent's inability to structure work so that anticipated requirements do not invalidate it (Jiang et al., arXiv:2609.03028, 2026-09-02).

evidence.title: Requirements After the First Edit: Mining Late Requirement Emergence and Rework in Real-World Coding-Agent Sessions
evidence.summary: 3,553 real coding-agent sessions: late-arriving requirements are followed by ~2x invalidation of prior edits vs matched non-requirement edits; advance warning of the requirement produced no measurable effect on overwriting in a controlled experiment.
